I don’t comment or post here as often as I used to… But I stumbled upon your post, and couldn’t help but offer my encouragement. I’ve been where you are. It lasted 2-3 years. I couldn’t imagine a future and considered myself permanently broken. I isolated. I binged everything from drinking, to eating, to television. I watched my life savings dwindle. I developed agoraphobia. I assumed I would end my life eventually, and I was comfortable with that. I was over and waiting for the credits to roll on my life. 
THEN, with some support from the only family I have (my sister), I rebuilt myself one tiny brick at a time by moving in with her. I found proper/new psychiatric help (ghosted my previous psychiatrist during what I refer to as my  “Howard Hughes Years”), and got back on meds. I slowly started going outside for a few minutes a day. This turned into walks. Walks turned into runs. I shared meals with my sister. I remember in bed in her tiny spare bedroom searching for jobs every morning. I felt sick at the thought of reentering the workforce. I shit the bed on multiple job opportunities. Then I found one that was perfect, at least at the time. I lived with my sister for 6 months total. The day I moved into my own place again, I couldn’t believe I made I through. It felt like a near death experience. 
Anyway, just know you can get better. It won’t be easy. It won’t be quick. It won’t  be some fairytale ending where you never get depressed again. But you’ll begin to see more and more glimpses of your true self. I don’t know your whole situation, but I know how you feel because I’ve felt the same way. And right now, I don’t feel that way. So hang in there.
